original_question: For n-dimensional continued fractions in dimensions n >= 3, determine which faces have the highest relative frequencies.
target_in_paper: Section 3.4, Problem 15: "Find frequencies on n-dimensional continued fractions with the highest relative frequencies," read together with the immediately preceding discussion of geometric relative frequencies via Möbius measure and the immediately following Problem 16, which makes clear that the objects being counted are faces up to integer congruence.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right part of the paper: the sail-statistics problem for higher-dimensional continued fractions, and it correctly focuses on dimensions n >= 3 and on determining which face types are most frequent.
missing_details: The paper is about geometric multidimensional continued fractions, not arbitrary multidimensional continued fraction algorithms.
The relevant geometric objects are faces of sails associated to arrangements of hyperplanes through the origin in R^n with the integer lattice Z^n, as introduced in Definition 2.2.

The comparison should be made between face types up to integer congruence (equivalently, integer-congruence classes of faces), which is clarified by the surrounding discussion and especially Problem 16.

The phrase "relative frequency" in this paper means geometric relative frequency defined via Möbius geometry: one integrates the infinitesimal cross-ratio against the projectively invariant Möbius measure on the space of arrangements.
The scope is the higher-dimensional case open for n > 2, i.e. n >= 3, not the classical two-dimensional case.
The paper does not narrow Problem 15 to only Klein sails or only Minkowski-Voronoi sails in its statement; restricting to one subclass would change the scope.
To make the question stand-alone, it should explicitly say that one seeks the face types attaining maximal relative frequency, rather than speaking only of "highest relative frequencies" abstractly.
refined_question: For each integer n >= 3, in the setting of geometric n-dimensional continued fractions in R^n with lattice Z^n - that is, sails of arrangements of n hyperplanes through the origin in general position in the sense of Definition 2.2 - determine which integer-congruence classes of faces of these sails attain the maximal geometric relative frequency, where relative frequency is the Möbius-geometric frequency defined in Section 3.4 by integrating the infinitesimal cross-ratio over the space of arrangements.
justification: The draft is closest to Problem 15 in Section 3.4, not to the neighboring Problems 16-18. Section 3.1 identifies "study the face distribution of sails" as the relevant statistical direction, Section 3.4 explains that the paper's notion of relative frequency is the Möbius/projectively invariant one on the space of arrangements, and Problem 16 immediately clarifies that the counted objects are faces considered up to integer non-congruence. So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is to ask for the integer-congruence classes of sail faces with maximal Möbius relative frequency in each dimension n >= 3, without drifting into the separate finiteness question of Problem 16, the summability question of Problem 17, or the Gauss-map question of Problem 18.
